name: Mission Control chat pane (per box)
cadence: on demand (via a Mission Control chat hand-off from bin/poll-commands.sh; no cron line)

knobs.note: 0 makes the Mission Control chat pane on this box call no model at all: the claude rung (bin/claude-cost.sh) and the fallback rung (bin/agent-call.sh) are refused BEFORE the vendor call with a zero-cost row_source=refused row, and the pane gets the bash rung's one reply.

Comma/space list of the ONLY runners the chat pane may reach. Empty is every runner, i.e. today's ladder unchanged. The claude rung is runner claude; the fallback rung is RUNNER_CHAT_FALLBACK through bin/agent-call.sh. A runner outside the list is refused before the call.

Dollars the chat pane may spend in the current UTC day, summed from D1 cost_rows stamped lane_id=box-chat through GET /api/metrics/llm-spend, never from the box's own logs/cost.csv. Checked before both the claude rung and the fallback rung.

Seconds one chat turn may run (each claude rung and the fallback rung), and how long a second question waits for the per-project turn lock before it is answered busy. Read as ${BOX_CHAT_TIMEOUT:-900}.
Empty by default: the model is the model_routes row for role orchestrate (bin/lib/lane-model.sh, ORCHESTRATOR_MODEL wins over it). Set this in env/global.env only to override that row on one box.

The runner the fallback rung hands to bin/agent-call.sh when the claude rung fails. Empty falls back to RUNNER_TRIAGE_FALLBACK, and both empty means no fallback rung. Registered so it is visible; set it in env/global.env on the box.
Read here only as the second choice for the chat fallback runner (${RUNNER_CHAT_FALLBACK:-${RUNNER_TRIAGE_FALLBACK:-}}). Set it in env/global.env on the box.
